Params: The composer's wife appears with a wheelchair. Beyond her elegant attire, she wears gloves and a mask, with a syringe in hand, her movements practiced and precise.
Bound by multiple restraints, the composer slumps in his wheelchair, blood seeping from the bandages around his head. His eyes bulge, vacant and lifeless.
His scarred wrists are hooked up to IV bags, but it is unclear whether they contain blood plasma or nutrients.
Having stumbled upon the host's secret, you two take a few steps back.
I knew getting that score wouldn't be easy. Nothing ever is easy in Xoth!
Just hold on a little longer.
The composer's wife holds the syringe up to the light, tapping it gently to gather air bubbles at the tip before expelling them.
The air hangs heavy with the scent of roses, their lush beauty masking the encroaching touch of death.
Relax, I have no intention of causing trouble for you. Besides, you're all newcomers here... surely you could use some help from a "local," no?
The wife tosses a stack of sheet music onto the table.
In exchange, I'd like to ask you to help us.
Karenina slips a detonator into your hand.
We're not agreeing to anything until you tell us why you defected.
Quite touchy about that, I see. I wonder... is that Purifying Force still led by that beautiful woman?
Have a seat, you two. Let's talk.
There's no benefit to making a scene here.
Neither Karenina nor you act, but you both edge closer to a window that you consider to be the best escape route.
I know you're cautious. That's why I'm not going to feed you some lie.
Like any household, we had our roles. The composer handled the fantasy and romance, while I dealt with reality and finances.
We were good together at first, you know. If the virus hadn't broken out... we could've been happy.
Struggling to survive in the conservation area... I started thinking about working on Babylonia.
Even as she speaks fondly of the past, the wife drives a syringe into her husband's neck. He claws at the armrest, his pupils dilating.
What, you think I would hurt him? I would never. This is just nutrient solution to keep him alive. Trust me... no one wants him to live more than I do.
But let's get back to our story. When did everything start falling apart? I'd say it was when the notice for the Construct modification came—
Out of everyone vying for the job, Construct workers are preferred to handle the grunt work.
We both signed up for it in hopes of obtaining the stability we'd always dreamed of. But I tested negative for Tantalum affinity, and I couldn't undergo the operation.
She caresses her husband's face. Sometimes, love looks no different from a curse.
But he could, so he went through with it. And as his wife, I got to join Babylonia too.
After that, I changed. I aged. My body, my energy, my mind... everything grew old.
But him? He was frozen in his twenties forever. Laughing, singing, making new friends, wanting to see new places.
A Construct and a human in love... just like you two. You think you'll be any different?
Across the long table, the four of you stand like mirrored images, except one pair has already reached the end, while the other hasn't even begun the journey.
You won't. Once a crack forms, it only widens.
You're just avoiding the problem until you have no choice but to face it. Luckily for me, I found a solution.
That's right. Here, I regained my youth with the power of the projection.
I didn't envy him anymore. I was no longer paranoid. And I was no longer in pain.
But at what cost? Construct defectors will get hunted down by the Purifying Force.
You gave up a normal life and went rogue... for this?
The wife doubles over with laughter, as if she has just heard the funniest joke in the world.
A "normal life"! You said a "normal life"! Hahaha... haha.
"Normal life" stopped existing the day the Punishing Virus broke out.
Or maybe it never existed in the first place. The Punishing Virus just made it obvious.
This place isn't any different from the outside world. We just traded one kind of madness for another.
At least this madness gave me what I crave.
Hmph. So coming here solved all your problems?!
The current state of the composer clearly suggests that something else happened after that.
Things were fine at first. Everything felt new and fresh to us, and we felt like we had gone back to when our relationship was at its best.
If only he hadn't wanted to leave me. He grew tired of this virtual world... or maybe he just grew tired of me.
Do you know that my husband is a real escape artist? He's tried to run away so many times, and he came close more than once.
Karenina's voice stays calm, but her fingers clench tight, her knuckles turning pale beneath her synthetic skin.
I "edited" his memories. Every time, I rewound it to the beginning, to the moment I thought was right.
Until eventually, I turned him into this without even realizing it.
No matter how you look at it, this has become a complete and utter tragedy.
Neither the people involved nor any outside observer can untangle this mess anymore.
What do you want us to do?
You do your best to keep your voice neutral and objective, without a trace of judgment.
You're the only one who can help us. Back when we were in Babylonia, I heard your name from the other Constructs who defected... 【kuroname】.
The constant damage caused his M.I.N.D. to deviate. He started showing manic, self-destructive tendencies, and that's why I've restrained him.
I haven't been able to wake him since last time. It's like his sight, hearing, and touch has been stripped away.
He's still here, but I can't feel him anymore. Not even a trace.
After all that time, all that love and hatred, he is fully hers finally. It is a shame that he is nothing but an empty shell now.
Karenina can almost see fate's mocking smile. There is no mercy here, just one endless tragedy after another.
I need you to help me wake him up. You're different. You're a human with a Mind Beacon connection that can't be corrupted.
Unauthorized M.I.N.D. connections are against protocol! You think there's no risk to the commandant doing this?
What if 【kuroname】's Mind Beacon gets infected? We're not in Babylonia. What if something goes wrong?
You can't guarantee this connection will be safe!
It will be. My husband is a gentle man... he'd sooner hurt himself than lay hands on someone else.
Before Karenina can say something more hurtful, you pull her toward you by the shoulder.
She turns back angrily, indignation flashing in her eyes.
Karenina presses her lips together, biting back her objections and protests.
I have to do something. I won't accept this. I can't just watch him die.
Whether he wants to leave or stay, I will let go after this.
She kneels on the ground, her shoulders trembling while she sobs silently, but only blood comes out now.
It doesn't take a medical degree to see the composer's in bad shape.
Truth be told, you are not even sure this will work. Connecting to a Construct with a damaged M.I.N.D. is something you rarely do, let alone performing it inside a projection like this.
But if you do nothing, the outcome is clear... a slow death for the Construct.
I'm not doing this for you.
I'm doing this to save him.
I can't promise this will end well.
Before you enter the connection, Karenina stays behind.
She refuses to wait with the composer's wife. It's hard to imagine what would happen if those two were left in a room together.
I'm going to stay here and watch over you until the connection's done... But don't get too emotional on me. I'm still mad at you.
And don't act tough if anything goes wrong in there. Cut the connection right away, got it?
You're the one who likes to act tough.
Karenina rambles on with her instructions. You realize you have never had the chance to watch her quietly like this.
Her soft hair falls loose and frames her face, her synthetic skin bearing a fine, peach-like texture. Her lashes cast delicate shadows, tracing her eyes like lace.
This will be the last sight you see before the connection, and the first one afterward.
You have never entered a M.I.N.D. this pale and calm, even if it's nothing but ruins.
Feathers scatter across the ground, and a wheelchair sits empty. Faintly glowing shards drift by occasionally.
I'm leaving. You can't stop me this time.
Impossible. There's no way you can awaken Carcosa. Unless...
Come with me. To the new world, to the outside world, to get captured by the Purifying Force... I don't care.
I can't stay here anymore. I really can't.
The Song of True Love... So Carcosa really can be awakened. We just failed.
I don't know... I really don't... Please, stop thinking about it... Just stop.
The composer sets down his suitcase and walks to his wife. He kneels, resting his head on her lap.
I'm not leaving anymore. I'm staying with you. We'll never be apart again.
He embraces his wife, but she raises a knife.
Just for your duty? Is that it?
In a beautiful little chapel, the bride adjusts the groom's collar. There are flowers, doves, champagne, and laughter.
Do you swear to stay by each other's side when you are needed the most, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health, in good times and in bad, till death do you part?
This is the only shard of happiness. Mixed in with the other shards, it hardly stands out at all.
Every shard after that is just the same damage being repeated. When the feathers are dyed completely red, they outline the shape of the composer.
The storms around you gradually subside, and Karenina and the room outside come into view. It seems that the <phonetic=M.I.N.D. Host>composer</phonetic> has regained a sliver of consciousness.
He raises a finger to his lips, shaking his head as he looks outside. Then he draws his finger across his throat like a blade.
Then he topples to the ground, dissolving back into feathers.
The composer chooses to remain unconscious and retreats into a self-imposed lockdown.
You shake your head. The connection did not last long, but the emotions it stirred up are a tangled mess. Conflicting feelings churn endlessly in you.
The composer's wife steps forward. You shake your head, giving her an apologetic look.
You should go. The score is on the desk. It's the last piece he composed... after watching your performance.
I'm sure... the two of you will do it justice.
Thinking back to the Corrupted at the base entrance, you believe you may get some answers from her.
The "kin" who left... have they sent word back?
Not once. He always kept tabs on the people who left for space... even after he got        "sick."
But the flight paths kept changing, and no word ever reached us.
Everything is quiet. By the time you step out of the composer's estate, night has already fallen.
Even on the darkest night, that sliver of moonlight still follows you like a shadow.
You move quickly, trying to put distance between yourself and that oppressive atmosphere.
Karenina suddenly speaks up when you cross the bridge. Lowering her head, she hides her expression in the shadow, but you can sense how serious she is.
Commandant... what do you think drove them to this point?
They feared that they weren't good enough, that the other didn't care as much, and that speaking up first meant losing.
It's like... everyone is scared to be the one who speaks up first in every relationship. Right?
Karenina looks up, as if searching for something... but perhaps she already knows the answer.
Kiki wouldn't tell me what she was thinking, the mermaid never asked her lover, the composer's wife misunderstood the composer... Everyone.
We're never going to end up like that, even if you and I change one day.
There might be rough patches, misunderstandings, arguments, even silent treatments... but I'll find you and hash it out, no matter what.
Everyone craves understanding, yet they're all terrified of the truth. So they get lost in their worst assumptions, tearing themselves apart until there's nothing left.
And... that day, the mermaid asked me if I... if I liked you, Commandant...
What I said back then was true, but... I wasn't being completely honest!
In a way you did not expect, Karenina seizes control of the conversation with a courage that burns white-hot.
The person you think of when you're in danger. The person you want to share good news with. The person you turn to for comfort. The person who makes you smile just by crossing your mind.
Liking something is easy. It doesn't need a reason. Like how I like bombs, collecting records, arguing with everyone.
But this feeling is there, so why can't I just say it?
Karenina steps forward and grabs your arm, her brow furrowed in thought.
Mm... Maybe it'd be better if I just kept all these feelings to myself.
As Karenina finally lets those hidden feelings out, her emotions begin to settle.
But I couldn't! Once I became aware of it, I just couldn't act normal around you anymore, no matter how much I tried to hide it, deny it, avoid it...
I don't fear getting hurt or being rejected. What I fear is... regret.
I believe in you, Commandant. And I believe in myself.
Even if this doesn't go the way I want, I have to get it off my chest, or I'll go crazy.
That's just how I do things! So, Commandant, I... I...
Karenina closes her eyes, mustering every ounce of courage.
Here and now, she is caught in this tempestuous whirlpool with no way out.
Words give way to an embrace. It is impossible to tell who moved first, and it doesn't matter.
There exists a vast middle ground in every relationship, a space marked by fences called "boundaries."
Once that line is crossed, there is no going back. One must tread carefully and watch every step, or someone is bound to get hurt, and things can spiral beyond repair.

But feelings are like a monsoon that comes and goes as it pleases. If you miss the juncture and let the season pass by, you will never find yourself in that place again, and you will never feel the rain.
Not here. Not now. When you leave this place and return to the real world...
One more thing... Commandant, if those flights to outer space were really launched, why haven't they heard anything back?
Every tragedy leads back to the Choir. It's like their whole purpose isn't to awaken Carcosa at all, but to...
Something about what Karenina is about to do triggers an alarm in you, but she holds you tighter before you can stop her.
Mmh... Don't get mad, Commandant. It's too late now anyway.
I went ahead with Plan D...
No, it's too dangerous! It's not worth the risk.
Karenina releases her embrace, covering one eye with her hand while the other gazes into the distance.
I already shut off the visual module in one eye, and... just as I thought.
Karenina leans against you, furrowing her brow and breathing heavily, her eyes locked ahead.
Her pupil trembles. You wonder what she is seeing right now.
The real Xoth complex... and the virtual projection... they're overlapping.
They're both showing up through the one eye I've got left. It's still not stable, but at least... I can see it now.
She tries to act like nothing is wrong, but the condensation liquid beading at her temple and her trembling lips give her away.
Tch... This is harder than I thought...
You want to support her through this, no matter what. She should not need to face a moment like this alone.
Sigh, guess there's no other way. Looks like I'll have to show you the truth like this.
Karenina, caught between overlapping realities, reaches out her hand.
M.I.N.D. overheated. Signal reception overloaded. Connection failed...
M.I.N.D. overheated. Signal reception overloaded. Connection failed...
M.I.N.D. overheating. Attempting to synchronize signals...
Signal synchronization at 98.95%... M.I.N.D. connection established.
